repo.name: Logos Apps (vpavlin)
repo.description: Public repo for vpavlin Logos apps (QAKU + more).

application.name: Kith
application.summary: Your people — a local-first, p2p address book on Loam
application.desc: Kith is the contacts app of the Loam ecosystem: a local-first, peer-to-peer address book. A contact can carry a Loam identity, turning it into a grantable principal for other apps (Scala editors, Qaku admins). Books sync across your devices; import/export vCards.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: KYM — Know Your Money
application.summary: Local-first p2p zero-based budgeting on Logos
application.desc: KYM (Know Your Money) is a local-first, peer-to-peer zero-based budget you own. Shared household budgets sync directly between devices over Waku — no bank login, no server.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: Loam
application.summary: The shared node your local-first apps grow in — one Logos Delivery node per phone
application.desc: Loam is the soil your Logos apps grow in: one shared Logos Delivery node per phone, used by every app over IPC, so ten apps don't each run their own node. Per-app consent, end-to-end encrypted (Loam only ever moves sealed bytes), and an opt-in offline cache that holds a closed app's messages so it reopens without re-syncing. It also runs a Bluetooth LE mesh, so nearby phones sync with no internet at all.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: Perun
application.summary: Local-first GPS ride & run tracker that syncs to your Basecamp over Logos
application.desc: Record GPS rides and runs offline, annotate them with photos, and export a shareable cinematic route video. Local-first and peer-to-peer to Basecamp desktop over Logos — no account, no server.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: Scala
application.desc: Secure, server-less shared calendar on Logos/Loam: E2E-encrypted, multi-writer, offline-first. RSVP, recurring events, custom fields, .ics import/export, Keycard identity.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: Shrooms
application.summary: The mycelial mesh VPN — your devices, no coordinator
application.desc:
An encrypted overlay network between your own machines, with no coordination server to trust or run. Nodes find each other through the network's own gossip and move data directly between one another.
WireGuard carries the traffic. Peers find each other over Logos Messaging, which is used only for rendezvous — once a tunnel exists it keeps working whether or not the messaging network is reachable.
Addresses are derived from device keys, so there is nothing to allocate and no address collisions. Peers that cannot reach each other directly fall back to a relay, discovered from its own announcement rather than configured.
To join, scan the code that "shrooms invite" prints on a machine already on the mesh. The invite is good for one device and fifteen minutes, and brings back a membership credential signed for this phone's own keys. A network key still works where there is no invite to scan.
Prototype.
application.author: vpavlin

application.name: WhisperBox
application.summary: Encrypted forms: answers sealed to the form's creator, on Loam
application.desc: Local-first, end-to-end-encrypted forms on Logos/Loam. Every answer is sealed to the form's key and carries no respondent identity on the wire. Anonymous or members-only forms, co-owners, quizzes, private replies, CSV export. No Google services.
application.author: vpavlin
